BiblicalUsage: Ga'on is majesty and pride together — God's excellency on one side, man's arrogance on the other. The LORD overthrew Pharaoh in the greatness of His excellency in Exodus 15:7, but He swears He abhors the excellency of Jacob in Amos 6:8, and the pride of Israel testifies to his face in Hosea 5:5. Sodom's pride, fullness of bread, and idleness are named as her iniquity in Ezekiel 16:49.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe excellency belongs to God alone, and when men claim it, it turns to pride. Pharaoh's army drowned in the greatness of God's excellency, and Sodom fell to the pride of hers. I hold that the difference between worship and ruin is knowing whose glory it is.
